title: Lemon rice
desc: Tangy South Indian rice with a crunchy peanut and dal tempering. The acidity helps it travel, and it tastes as good at room temperature as it does hot.
steps: Spread the cooled rice on a plate and break up any lumps so every grain takes the tempering.
Heat the oil and add mustard seeds. When they pop, add chana dal, urad dal and peanuts and fry until golden.
Add the chilli, curry leaves, hing and turmeric. Stir for 20 seconds on medium heat so the turmeric does not scorch.
Tip in the rice and salt and fold gently for 2 minutes.
Turn off the heat, then stir in the lemon juice. Adding it off the heat keeps it bright instead of bitter.
Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours settle before you pack.
pack: Pack it warm, not steaming, so the lid does not sweat and turn the rice soggy. Add cucumber slices or a small tin of curd with an ice pack.
swap: Use cooked millets or quinoa instead of rice. For nut-free schools, skip the peanuts and add roasted chana dal.

title: Vegetable pulao
desc: Fragrant basmati with whole spices and mixed vegetables. A one-pot office tiffin that reheats well and needs only a raita or salad beside it.
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs almost clear, then soak it for 20 minutes and drain.
Heat the ghee and add the bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon and cumin. Let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onion and cook until light golden, then stir in the ginger-garlic paste for 30 seconds.
Add the vegetables and cook for 2 minutes, then add the rice and stir gently for 1 minute.
Pour in the water with salt, bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes (or 2 whistles in a pressure cooker).
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
pack: For a hot tiffin, fill your insulated tin with boiling water for a few minutes, empty it, then add the pulao while it is still steaming and close it straight away.
swap: Add paneer cubes or chickpeas for protein. For a Jain tiffin, skip the onion, garlic, ginger and carrot and use peas, beans and capsicum.

title: Paneer kathi roll
desc: Spiced, seared paneer rolled in a soft roti with onion, capsicum and mint chutney. Hand-held, mess-free and the most traded item in any school tiffin.
steps: Mix the curd, chilli powder, garam masala, ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice and salt. Coat the paneer and leave for 15 minutes.
Sear the paneer in a hot oiled pan for about 2 minutes a side until charred at the edges.
Toss the capsicum in the same pan for 1 minute so it stays crisp.
Warm the rotis and spread a thin layer of mint chutney on each.
Add paneer, onion and capsicum, sprinkle chaat masala and roll tightly.
Wrap each roll in butter paper or foil and twist the ends.
pack: Paneer and a curd marinade are perishable, so pack the rolls with an ice pack. The butter-paper wrap keeps the chutney inside the roll, not on the tin.
swap: Use firm tofu for a vegan roll. Leftover chapatis work as well as fresh rotis.

title: Aloo paratha
desc: Whole-wheat flatbread stuffed with spiced potato and cooked with ghee. Stack them with pickle and curd and you have a Punjabi tiffin that needs nothing else.
steps: Knead the flour and water into a soft dough and rest it for 20 minutes.
Mash the potatoes completely with the chilli, coriander, ajwain, amchur, garam masala and salt. Lumps tear the dough, so mash until smooth.
Divide the dough and the filling into 4 portions each.
Roll a dough ball into a small disc, put the filling in the centre, pleat the edges together and seal. Flatten, dust with flour and roll gently into a 7-inch circle.
Cook on a hot tawa. Flip when small bubbles appear, spread ghee on both sides and press until golden spots form.
Cool on a rack for 5 minutes before stacking.
pack: Cooling on a rack lets the steam escape so the parathas stay soft rather than leathery. Stack with butter paper between them and pack curd separately with an ice pack.
swap: Fill with grated paneer or cauliflower instead. For a Jain paratha, use mashed raw banana in place of potato.

title: Egg bhurji wrap
desc: Indian-style scrambled eggs with onion, tomato and pav bhaji masala, rolled in a roti. Fifteen minutes from fridge to tin.
ing: pav bhaji masala or garam masala
steps: Melt the butter and soften the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the chilli, tomato, turmeric, masala and salt and cook until the tomato breaks down, about 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs, pour them in and scramble on medium heat until fully set with no wet egg left.
Stir in the coriander and let the bhurji cool for 5 minutes.
Spoon onto the rotis and roll tightly.
pack: Cook the eggs all the way through. Soft, runny eggs are lovely at home but not in a tiffin. Wrap in foil and pack with an ice pack.
swap: For a vegetarian version, make the paneer bhurji variation by crumbling 200 g paneer in place of the eggs.

title: Dry chana masala
desc: Chickpeas cooked until the masala clings. No gravy means no leaks, and it pairs with rotis, rice or a simple salad.
steps: Heat the oil and let the cumin seeds crackle.
Add the onion and cook until golden, about 6 minutes, then the ginger-garlic paste and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the tomato puree, chana masala, chilli powder, turmeric and salt. Cook until the oil separates, about 5 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and a quarter cup of water. Mash a few chickpeas against the pan to thicken.
Simmer uncovered for about 8 minutes until the masala coats the chickpeas and the pan looks almost dry.
Finish with amchur and coriander.
pack: Pack it beside jeera rice or two rotis, with onion rings and a lemon wedge in a small separate tin.
swap: Stir in a handful of spinach at the end. For a Jain tiffin, skip the onion, garlic and ginger and lean on tomato, hing and amchur.

title: Rajma chawal
desc: Slow-simmered kidney beans in an onion-tomato masala with plain rice. The Sunday-lunch classic, batch-cooked for the week.
steps: Drain the soaked beans and pressure cook them in fresh water with salt for 6 to 7 whistles, until one crushes easily between your fingers. Dried kidney beans must reach a hard boil: never slow-cook them from raw.
Heat the oil with cumin seeds and the bay leaf, then cook the onion until deep golden.
Add the ginger-garlic paste for a minute, then the tomato puree and the powders. Cook until the oil separates.
Add the beans with their cooking liquid and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing a few beans to thicken.
Finish with garam masala.
pack: Pack the rajma and the rice in separate tiers so the rice does not go mushy. Preheat the insulated tin with boiling water and pack both piping hot.
swap: Use two cans of kidney beans to bring the time down to about 25 minutes.

title: Vegetable upma
desc: Roasted semolina cooked with a South Indian tempering and finely chopped vegetables. Soft, savoury and ready in twenty minutes.
steps: Dry-roast the rava on medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes until it smells nutty but has not browned. Set aside.
Heat the ghee and oil and temper the mustard seeds, urad dal, chana dal, curry leaves, chilli and ginger.
Cook the onion for 2 minutes and the vegetables for 3 more.
Add the water and salt and bring to a rolling boil.
Lower the heat and pour in the rava in a thin stream, stirring all the time so no lumps form.
Cover for 2 minutes, then finish with lemon juice and coriander.
pack: Upma firms up as it cools, so make it slightly looser than you would serve at home. It will be soft, not stiff, by lunchtime.
swap: Use millet rava or broken wheat (dalia) with 3 cups of water.

title: Kanda poha
desc: Flattened rice with onion, peanuts and curry leaves, finished with lemon. Maharashtra's favourite breakfast doubles as a light, quick tiffin.
steps: Rinse the poha twice in a colander under running water. Do not soak it.
Sprinkle salt, sugar and turmeric over the damp poha, toss and leave for 5 minutes.
Fry the peanuts in the oil until crisp and lift them out.
In the same oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves and chilli, then the onion until translucent.
If using potato, add it now, cover and cook for about 6 minutes until tender.
Add the poha and stir gently on low heat for 2 minutes, cover for 2 more, then finish with lemon, coriander and the peanuts.
pack: Pack the sev and a lemon wedge in a small separate tin, so the poha stays fluffy and the sev stays crunchy.
swap: For a Jain tiffin, skip the onion and potato and add peas and pomegranate after cooking.

title: Mini idli with podi
desc: Bite-sized steamed idlis tossed in ghee and spiced lentil podi. Finger food that does not stick together or need a chutney.
steps: Grease the mini idli moulds and stir the batter gently without knocking out the air.
Fill each mould about three-quarters full.
Steam for 10 to 12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Rest for 2 minutes, then unmould with a wet spoon.
Warm the ghee with the curry leaves, then toss the idlis with the podi until every one is coated.
pack: The ghee and podi coating stops the idlis sticking together. Let them cool before closing the lid. Coconut chutney spoils fast, so pack it with an ice pack or leave it out.
swap: Store-bought batter works fine. For very young children, halve the podi.

title: Methi thepla
desc: Soft Gujarati flatbreads made with fenugreek leaves, curd and spices. The original travel tiffin, made to last through a long day.
steps: Mix everything except the water.
Add water a little at a time and knead to a firm but soft dough.
Rest the dough for 15 minutes, then divide into about 12 balls.
Roll each ball thin.
Cook on a hot tawa with a few drops of oil on each side until brown spots appear.
Stack the theplas in a clean cloth while you finish the batch to keep them soft.
pack: Cooked through with curd and oil and kept dry, thepla is the tiffin Gujarati families pack for train journeys. Pair it with pickle and a dry potato sabzi.
swap: For vegan theplas, replace the curd with water and a teaspoon of lemon juice.

title: Curd rice
desc: Soft rice folded into curd with a mustard and curry-leaf tempering. Cooling and gentle, with a splash of milk so it does not sour by lunch.
steps: Mash the warm rice lightly with a spoon, then let it cool completely.
Stir in the curd, milk and salt. The milk keeps it from turning sour by lunchtime.
Heat the oil and temper the mustard seeds, urad dal, curry leaves and hing.
Pour the tempering over the rice with the ginger and chilli and fold through.
Top with carrot or cucumber and pomegranate.
pack: Pack it cold with an ice pack and eat it within four hours. It is the right tiffin for a hot day, not for a radiator-side locker.
swap: Use cooked millet instead of rice. For a Jain tiffin, skip the ginger, chilli and carrot.

title: Chicken tikka wrap
desc: Yoghurt-marinated chicken thigh, charred in a pan or air fryer, wrapped with onion, crunchy cabbage and mint chutney.
steps: Mix the yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste, spices, lemon juice, oil and salt. Coat the chicken and marinate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight in the fridge.
Cook in a very hot pan for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, or in an air fryer at 200°C for 12 to 14 minutes.
Check the thickest piece: chicken is done at 74°C (165°F) in the centre.
Let it rest and cool for 5 minutes.
Spread chutney on each roti, add the chicken, onion and cabbage and roll tightly.
pack: Cool the chicken before rolling so the wrap does not steam itself soggy, and pack it with two cold sources, such as an ice pack and a frozen water bottle.
swap: Make the paneer kathi roll for a vegetarian version of the same tiffin.

title: Egg fried rice
desc: Indo-Chinese fried rice with scrambled egg, crunchy vegetables, garlic and soy. A good home for yesterday's rice if it was stored properly.
steps: Use rice that was cooled quickly after cooking and kept in the fridge for no more than a day.
Scramble the eggs in half the oil until fully set, then lift them out.
Heat the rest of the oil on high and stir-fry the garlic and vegetables for 2 minutes.
Add the rice, soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and salt and toss for 3 minutes until every grain is hot.
Fold the eggs back in and finish with spring onion.
pack: Cooked rice that sits warm can grow bacteria whose toxins survive reheating. Either pack it steaming hot in a preheated insulated tin, or cool it fast and pack it cold with an ice pack.
swap: Use paneer or tofu cubes for an egg-free version.

title: Veg hakka noodles
desc: Wok-tossed noodles with crisp julienned vegetables, soy and chilli sauce. The tiffin most children ask for by name.
steps: Boil the noodles for one minute less than the packet says, rinse in cold water and toss with a teaspoon of oil.
Heat the remaining oil on high and stir-fry the garlic and onion for 30 seconds.
Add the vegetables and stir-fry for 2 minutes so they keep their crunch.
Add the noodles, sauces, vinegar, pepper and salt and toss with tongs for 2 minutes.
Finish with spring onion.
pack: Undercooking the noodles by a minute matters: they keep softening in the tin. The oil toss stops them clumping by lunch.
swap: Add scrambled egg or shredded chicken for a non-veg version.

title: Moong dal khichdi
desc: Rice and yellow moong dal cooked soft with ghee, cumin and ginger. Gentle comfort food that fills a tiffin and an afternoon.
steps: Wash the rice and dal together until the water runs clear, then soak for 15 minutes.
Heat the ghee and add the cumin, hing and ginger.
Add the drained rice and dal, vegetables, turmeric, salt and water.
Pressure cook for 3 whistles, or simmer covered for about 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Mash lightly and loosen with hot water: khichdi thickens a lot as it cools.
pack: Make it looser than you would serve at the table. Pack it piping hot in a preheated insulated tin, with papad and pickle in a separate dry tin.
swap: Use broken wheat or millet in place of rice.

title: Bombay masala sandwich
desc: Buttered bread layered with green chutney, potato, cucumber, tomato and sandwich masala. Toast it and it stays crisp until lunch.
steps: Butter each slice right to the edges. The butter is the barrier that keeps the bread from going soggy.
Spread a thin layer of chutney over the butter.
Pat the tomato and cucumber dry with kitchen paper.
Layer the potato, cucumber, tomato and onion, sprinkling masala and salt between layers.
Close, press down and toast in a sandwich maker or pan if you are packing it for more than two hours.
Cut into quarters.
pack: Toasted bread holds juicy vegetables much better than soft bread. Wrap the quarters snugly in butter paper so they do not slide apart.
swap: Add a slice of cheese, or swap the potato for boiled beetroot.

title: Moong dal chilla
desc: Savoury pancakes made from soaked yellow moong dal. High in protein, naturally gluten-free and quick once the dal is soaked.
steps: Drain the dal and grind it with the chilli, ginger and a little water to a smooth, thick, pourable batter.
Stir in the turmeric, hing, salt, onion and coriander.
Ladle the batter onto a hot greased tawa and spread it into a thin circle.
Drizzle oil around the edge and cook for about 2 minutes until the edges lift.
Flip and cook for 1 more minute.
pack: Fold each chilla in quarters and stack with paper between them. Pack the green chutney cold in a small tin.
swap: Stuff the chillas with grated paneer for children, or add grated vegetables to the batter.

title: Jain cabbage capsicum sabzi
desc: A dry Gujarati-style stir-fry with no onion, garlic or root vegetables, finished with roasted peanut powder and lemon.
steps: Heat the oil and add the mustard seeds, cumin and hing.
Add the cabbage, capsicum, turmeric and salt.
Stir-fry uncovered on medium-high heat for 6 to 7 minutes. Leaving the lid off stops it turning watery.
Add the coriander powder, chilli powder and sugar and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the peanut powder, then turn off the heat and add the lemon juice and coriander.
pack: A dry sabzi means no leaks. Pack it with theplas or rotis and a small tin of curd with an ice pack.
swap: Add boiled green peas. Some hing is blended with wheat flour, so check the pack if you need it gluten-free.

title: Sprouts chaat salad
desc: Steamed moong sprouts with cucumber, tomato and onion, dressed with lemon and chaat masala at lunch so it stays crunchy.
steps: Steam the sprouts for 3 to 4 minutes, then cool them completely. Health agencies advise children, older adults and anyone pregnant not to eat raw sprouts.
Mix the sprouts with cucumber, tomato, onion, chilli, coriander and pomegranate.
In a tiny jar, mix the lemon juice, chaat masala, cumin and salt.
Pack the dressing separately and pour it over just before eating.
pack: Keep it cold with an ice pack and dress it at lunch so the vegetables do not weep into the sprouts.
swap: Add boiled chickpeas or roasted peanuts to make it more filling.

title: Chicken keema matar
desc: Spiced chicken mince with green peas, cooked dry enough to pack. Good with rotis, pav or jeera rice.
steps: Heat the oil and crackle the cumin seeds, then cook the onion until golden, about 6 minutes.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and chilli for 1 minute.
Add the mince and break it up with a spoon. Cook on high until no pink remains, about 6 minutes.
Add the powders and tomato puree and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the peas and a quarter cup of water, cover and cook for 8 minutes, then uncover and cook until almost dry.
Finish with garam masala and coriander. Mince should reach 74°C (165°F).
pack: Cook it dry so it cannot leak, and pack it piping hot in a preheated insulated tin with rotis wrapped separately.
swap: Use soya granules (soaked and squeezed) for a vegetarian keema.
